title: Research Study on Improved Prediction of CNS Recurrence in Aggressive B-Cell Lymphomas Through Detection of Circulating Tumor DNA in Cerebrospinal Fluid (ID_CNSL)
summary:
This research study is conducted to develop novel molecular methods to improve the prediction of central nervous system (CNS) relapses in aggressive B-cell lymphomas.
A CNS relapse of aggressive B-cell lymphomas is a severe event associated with a poor prognosis. It affects approximately 5% of all patients with DLBCL/HGBCL (DLBCL = Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma; HGBCL = High-Grade B-Cell Lymphoma). At present, it is extremely difficult to predict which patients will experience a CNS relapse, as currently used diagnostic methods are not sufficiently suited for this purpose. This means they lack the sensitivity to detect the smallest lymphoma cells within the CNS. Therefore, the primary objective of this research study is to develop and apply novel, improved methods capable of identifying patients at a particularly high risk for a CNS relapse. If successful, this could potentially enable the use of tailored and personalized therapies in the future to prevent CNS relapses.
This research study investigates whether circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) represents a biomarker that allows for an improved prediction of CNS relapse. ctDNA consists of minute fragments of the tumor's genetic information, which can be detected in body fluids using state-of-the-art methods. In our laboratory, we have developed a method that can detect ctDNA with ultra-sensitivity in the cerebrospinal fluid. In this research project, we will investigate whether this technology can be utilized for future predictions. The biomaterials will be collected from all 200 participants, stored in a study-specific manner, and molecularly analyzed.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Diagnosis or high clinical suspicion of:
• DLBCL, NOS (Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma, not otherwise specified) with a CNS-IPI score of 4–6
• High-grade B-cell lymphoma, NOS
• High-grade B-cell lymphoma with MYC and BCL2 and/or BCL6 rearrangement (Double-Hit / Triple-Hit Lymphoma)
• DLBCL with testicular involvement
• DLBCL with breast involvement
- Indication for routine lumbar puncture: Patients undergoing a lumbar puncture as part of standard clinical routine to collect cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and rule out central nervous system (CNS) involvement by the lymphoma.
- Informed Consent: Written informed consent obtained from the patient in accordance with international guidelines (e.g., GCP/Declaration of Helsinki), and the capacity to understand the study characteristics and study-related procedures.
- Adequate Biomaterial Availability: It must be foreseeable that at least 3 mL of CSF, 30 mL of blood, and sufficient tumor tissue will be available for the research projects.
Exclusion criteria:
• Incapacity: Patients who lack legal capacity and are unable to understand the nature, significance, and consequences of the study.
• Manifest CNS Involvement: Patients with manifest CNS involvement by the lymphoma, determined by MRI and/or cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) analyses (cytopathology, immunophenotyping).
• Safety Risk: Presence of any medical condition or abnormality that, in the judgment of the investigator, would compromise the patient's safety.
• Dependency/Employment: Patients who are in a position of dependency or employment with the sponsor or the investigators.
• HIV Status: HIV-positive patients.
• Planned High-Dose Therapy: Patients for whom high-dose chemotherapy and autologous stem cell transplantation are planned as part of their therapeutic regimen.
